title: Fake passkey help desks, real cloud theft
overview: Microsoft details fake help-desk calls that let attackers enrol their own authentication methods and steal cloud data. There’s also a Sogou follow-up, vulnerable WordPress plugins and public router exploits, plus Chess.com data and an insider SIM-swap sentence.
paragraphs: [cheerful] Good morning, it's 5:22 AM. Monday, the fourteenth of September, twenty twenty-six. five twenty-two AM is brought to you by Lab five twenty-two, a technology partner for mid-market businesses, providing cyber security services and enterprise operational software. Email us at hello at lab five twenty-two dot co dot uk if you think we can help your business.

[serious] The help desk calls your personal phone: update your passkey now or lose access. Microsoft says that’s the opening to cloud intrusions it’s been detecting since May. The link leads to a counterfeit Microsoft sign-in, sometimes using device-code phishing. [short pause] In one incident, nobody needed to steal a password or a cookie. The victim authorised access on the attacker’s behalf. That’s not a broken passkey; it’s a convincing lie about setting one up.

[curious] Then comes the bit I’d hunt for first: an authentication method the user never added. Attackers enrol their own M-F-A for persistence, inventory the tenant through the Graph A-P-I, then collect files and mail for hours or days. Compromised accounts also send follow-on lures through Teams. [confident] Check unexpected enrolments after help-desk calls or texts and revoke the associated sessions. Treat unexpected device-code flows as suspicious, and correlate Graph activity with bulk downloads rather than judging each request alone. A company name before passkeyhelpdesk dot com doesn’t make it your help desk.

[serious] Microsoft also disclosed over a million executive-impersonation emails sent between the third and fifth of August, demanding A-C-H payments for a fake ServiceNow subscription. Fabricated conversations backed up the invoices; finance should verify those demands through a known channel. [curious] And on Saturday’s Sogou Input Method story, we now know a crafted S-G-biz link chains weaknesses into an unsandboxed Chromium eighty webview for one-click code execution. Confirm version 16 point 3 point 0 point 3498 or later: it restricts navigation to approved domains over H-T-T-P-S, but the engine remains outdated and unsandboxed, so I’d remove it where Chinese input isn’t needed.

[long pause] [serious] From a browser inside an app to missing permission checks on websites: WordPress’s CryptoPayment Gateway, versions 1 point 2 point 1 through 1 point 2 point 2, lets unauthenticated callers rewrite payment configuration and retrieve wallet credentials in cleartext; CVE-2026-81648 scores ten. No exploitation is cited and no fixed release is named, so disable it, rotate stored wallet credentials and check whether the configuration changed. [calm] Also on WordPress, unauthenticated stored cross-site scripting affects GenieWords 1 point 5 point 27 through 1 point 5 point 34 and Hoo Companion 1 point 0 point 2; YouTube Embed 10 point 0 through 10 point 3 is affected too, with all scoring eight point eight. No fixes are named: move beyond those versions where a release exists, otherwise remove them, and inspect stored content for injected scripts — Hoo’s import flaw also destroys existing theme settings.

[serious] The web interface on Totolink’s A3002MU router needs containing too: four remotely reachable buffer overflows in its boa server score nine point nine, require low privileges, and already have public exploits. No fixed firmware is named, so disable internet-facing management and restrict local admin access while planning replacement. [short pause] [calm] Away from exposed interfaces, Have I Been Pwned added Chess dot com data yesterday: seven point three million rows posted in August contained four point six million unique email addresses alongside profile details, with analysis suggesting scraping rather than a breach. No password exposure is stated; affected users should still replace reused passwords and enable two-factor authentication. And sometimes access is sold from inside: a former A-T-and-T retail worker has received sixteen months in federal prison for using his system access to hijack customers’ phone numbers for cybercriminals.

[confident] I’d give unexpected cloud authentication enrolments the first investigation slot today. For products with no named fix, containment is a decision you can make now, not something to leave waiting on a release note. [cheerful] Have a good Monday. five twenty-two AM, brought to you by Lab five twenty-two. Find us at lab five twenty-two dot co dot uk.
